''18. Gates of hel.''] Becau{{ls}}e the Church is re{{ls}}embled to a hou{{ls}}e or a citie, the aduer{{ls}}arie powers al{{ls}}o be likened to a contrarie hou{{ls}}e or towne, the gates wherof, that is to {{ls}}ay, the fortitude or impugnations {{ls}}hal neuer preuaile again{{ls}}t the citie of Chri{{ls}}t. And {{ls}}o by this promis we are a{{ls}}{{ls}}ured that no here{{ls}}ies nor other wicked attempts can preuaile again{{ls}}t the Church builded vpon Peter, which the Fathers call Peters {{ls}}ee and the Romane Church. ''Count'' ({{ls}}aith S. Augu{{ls}}tine{{outside L|''P{{ls}}al. cont. part. Donati.''}}) ''the Prie{{ls}}ts from the very See of Peter, and in that order of Fathers con{{ls}}ider who to whom hath {{ls}}ucceded, that {{ls}}ame is the rocke which the proud gates of Hel do not ouercome.'' ''19. To thee.''] In {{ls}}aying, ''to thee vvil I geue'', it is plaine that as he gaue the keies to him, {{ls}}o he builded the Church vpon him. So {{ls}}aith S. Cyprian{{outside L|''Cyp. epi{{ls}}t. 73. Greg. li. 4. ep. 32. ind. 12.''}}, ''To Peter fir{{ls}}t of al, vpon vvhom our Lord built the Church, and from vvhom he in{{ls}}tituted and {{ls}}hevved the beginning of vnitie, did he geue this povver, that that {{ls}}hould be loo{{ls}}ed in the heauens, vvhich he had loo{{ls}}ed in earth.'' Wherby appeareth the vaine cauil of our Aduer{{ls}}aries, which {{ls}}ay the Church was built vpon Peters Confe{{ls}}sion only, cōmon to him and the re{{ls}}t, and not vpon his per{{ls}}on, more then vpon the re{{ls}}t.

''19. The keies.''] {{outside R|The dignities of the keies.}}That is, The authoritie or Chaire of doctrine, knowledge, iudgement and di{{ls}}cretion betwene true and fal{{ls}}e doctrine: the height of gouernement, the power of making lawes, of calling Councels, of the principal voice in them, of confirming them, of making Canons and hole{{ls}}om decrees, of abrogating the contrarie, of ordaining Bi{{ls}}hopes and Pa{{ls}}tors or depo{{ls}}ing and {{ls}}u{{ls}}pending them, finally the power to di{{ls}}pen{{ls}}e the goods of the Church both {{ls}}piritual and temporal. Which {{ls}}ignification of preeminent power and authoritie by the vvord ''keies'' the Scripture expre{{ls}}{{ls}}eth in many places: namely {{ls}}peaking of Chri{{ls}}t, {{outside L|''Apoc. 1.''}}''I haue the keies of death and Hel, that is, the rule''. And againe, {{outside L|''E{{ls}}a. 22, 22.''}}''I wil geue the key of the hou{{ls}}e of Dauid vpon his {{ls}}houlder''. Moreouer it {{ls}}ignifieth that men can not come into heauen but by him, the keies {{ls}}ignifiing al{{ls}}o authoritie to open and {{ls}}hut, as it is {{ls}}aid ''Apoc. 3''. of Chri{{ls}}t, ''Who hath the key of Dauid, he {{ls}}hutteth and no man openeth''. By which wordes we gather that Peters authoritie is maruelous, to whom the keies, that is, the power to open and {{ls}}hut heauen, is geuen. And therfore by the name of keies is geuen that {{ls}}upereminent power which is called in compari{{ls}}on of the power graunted to other Apo{{ls}}tles, Bi{{ls}}hops aud Pa{{ls}}tors, ''plenitudo pote{{ls}}tatis'', fulnes of power. ''Bernard. lib. 2. de con{{ls}}iderat. c. 8''.

''19. What{{ls}}oeuer thou {{ls}}hal bind.''] Al kind of di{{ls}}cipline and puni{{ls}}hment of offenders, either {{ls}}piritual (which directly is here meant) or corporal {{ls}}o farre as it tendeth to the execution of the {{ls}}piritual charge, is compri{{ls}}ed vnder the word, bind. Of which {{ls}}ort be Excommunications, Anathemati{{ls}}mes, Su{{ls}}pen{{ls}}ions, degradations, and other cen{{ls}}ures and penalties or penances enioyned either in the Sacrament of Confe{{ls}}sion or in the exterior Courtes of the Church, for puni{{ls}}hment both of other crimes, and {{ls}}pecially of here{{ls}}ie and rebellion again{{ls}}t the Church and the cheefe pa{{ls}}tors therof.

''19. Loo{{ls}}e.''] To loo{{ls}}e, is as the cau{{ls}}e and the offenders ca{{ls}}e requireth, to loo{{ls}}e them of any the former bandes, and to re{{ls}}tore them to the Churches Sacraments and Communion of the faithful and execution of their function, to pardon al{{ls}}o either al or part of the penances enioyned, or what debtes {{ls}}o euer man oweth to God or the Church for the {{ls}}atisfaction of his {{ls}}innes forgeuen. Which kind of relea{{ls}}ing or loo{{ls}}ing is called ''Indulgence'': finally this ''what{{ls}}oeuer'', excepteth nothing that is puni{{ls}}hable or pardonable by Chri{{ls}}t in earth, for he hath committed his power to Peter. And {{ls}}o the validitie of Peters {{ls}}entence in binding or loo{{ls}}ing what{{ls}}oeuer, {{ls}}hal by Chri{{ls}}tes promis be ratified in heauen. ''Leo Ser. de Transfig. & Ser. 2. in anniuer{{ls}}. a{{ls}}{{ls}}umpt. ad Pontif. Hilar. can. 16. in Matth. Epiph. in Anchorato prope initium''. If now any temporal power can {{ls}}hew their warrant out of {{ls}}cripture for {{ls}}uch {{ls}}oueraine power, as is here geuen to Peter and con{{ls}}equently to his {{ls}}ucce{{ls}}{{ls}}ors, by the{{ls}}e wordes, ''what{{ls}}oeuer thou {{ls}}hal binde'', and by the very keies, wherby greate{{ls}}t {{ls}}oueraintie is {{ls}}ignified in Gods Church as in his familie and hou{{ls}}hold, and therfore principally attributed and geuen to Chri{{ls}}t * {{outside L|''E{{ls}}a. 22. Apoc. 3''.}} who in the {{ls}}cripture is {{ls}}aid to haue the key of Dauid, but here cōmunicated al{{ls}}o vnto Peter, as the name of Rocke: if I {{ls}}ay any temporal pote{{ls}}tate can {{ls}}hew authoritie for the like {{ls}}oueraintie, let them chalenge hardly to be head not only of one particular, but of the whole vniuer{{ls}}al Church.
